攻击路径分析

The underlying consequence remains high because successful interception exposes reusable machine and user identities, answer images, and scanner-submission integrity. Likelihood is medium rather than high because the vector is local-network, user interaction is required, local mode is the default, and a reachable LAN proxy or listener must exist despite the repository server binding to 127.0.0.1. The separate deployment guide's HTTPS requirement is meaningful counterevidence but is not dispositive because the in-product guide and placeholder explicitly recommend plaintext remote operation and the client does not enforce TLS. This is not hard-suppressed: the attacker is an unauthenticated lower-privileged LAN party, the impact is not self-only, and following the documented workflow is a plausible product action rather than an attacker needing privileged write access. Applying the required matrix mechanically, impact=high and likelihood=medium produces medium final criticality. The result remains reportable.

路径
Scanner operator following the in-product remote-mode guide --enters the documented HTTP URL and scanner key, then logs in or scans--> Scanner client configured with plaintext HTTP base URL --transmits authentication material and educational records without TLS--> Unauthenticated on-path school-LAN attacker --observes or modifies plaintext requests and responses--> Captured password, API key, bearer token, upload token, and answer image --replays valid scanner or user credentials and can alter scanner submissions--> Project-X login and scanner upload APIs

Attacker story: a school scanner operator follows the guide bundled into the application, configures http://192.168.1.100:5174 with an administrator-issued scanner key, and logs in or uploads answer cards. The URL is accepted without scheme validation. The production request helper then sends the password body, X-Api-Key, bearer token, per-page upload token, and scanned images over ordinary HTTP. An unauthenticated on-path LAN attacker can capture reusable credentials and educational records or alter scan traffic. The supplied executable validation exercised the production URL and header helper and observed each claimed data class at an HTTP receiver. Repository controls include loopback server binding, local mode as the default, scoped/revocable API keys, authenticated upload routes, and a separate deployment guide requiring HTTPS. Those controls reduce likelihood but do not protect a user who follows the conflicting in-product HTTP instructions. The issue is reportable because it crosses a real LAN trust boundary and compromises identities and student data; it is not a self-only, developer-only, or attacker-privileged path.

发生可能性
Medium - Exploitation is technically simple and requires no Project-X account once a plaintext remote endpoint is used, and the exact unsafe URL is promoted in both the bundled guide and UI placeholder. However, the attacker must be on the victim's LAN path, the operator must select remote rather than default local mode, and the repository's server binds only to loopback, requiring additional LAN ingress configuration. The conflicting HTTPS deployment guidance further reduces deployment prevalence. These facts support medium rather than high likelihood.
影响程度
High - Plaintext transmission can disclose reusable account passwords, bearer sessions, scanner API keys, upload tokens, and identifiable student answer images. Reuse of a scanner key permits authenticated scanner submissions, while reuse of a user credential or token grants that user's broader permissions. Active interception can affect scan integrity as well as confidentiality. This is a high-impact identity and educational-data compromise, although the affected population and privilege level depend on which operator account and key traverse the connection.
假设条件
A school operator follows the in-product scanner guide or matching login-page placeholder and configures a reachable plaintext LAN endpoint.
An unauthenticated attacker can observe or modify traffic on the scanner workstation's local network path.
Because the Node server binds to loopback, a separate operator-configured LAN listener or reverse proxy is required for the documented 192.168.1.100 endpoint to be reachable.
A scanner operator configures remote mode with a non-loopback HTTP URL.
The HTTP endpoint is made reachable on the school LAN.
The victim enters account credentials or uploads scans through that endpoint.
The attacker is on-path or otherwise able to observe or modify LAN traffic.
控制措施
The Node service binds to 127.0.0.1 rather than directly opening port 5174 on the LAN.
Local scanner mode is documented as the default.
A separate deployment guide recommends an HTTPS Nginx reverse proxy and expressly requires HTTPS in production.

These authentication and authorization controls do not provide transport confidentiality and accept credentials captured from plaintext traffic.
盲点
No repository manifest establishes a concrete LAN-facing listener, reverse proxy, load balancer, or deployment using the documented private address; the direct Node process is loopback-only.
The supplied PoC used an HTTP capture server rather than a separate physical school-LAN host or packet sniffer, although it exercised the production URL and request-header code.
The full TWAIN hardware workflow was not executed, but password and API-key exposure occurs independently of scanner hardware.
The exact number and privilege level of users likely to authenticate from scanner workstations cannot be determined statically.

概要

Introduced: the new process.cwd()-relative default is not backward-compatible with the previous module-relative path used by bundled standalone servers. Because the initialization path automatically creates a known bootstrap administrator when the newly selected database is empty, this is more than ordinary data-path breakage and can expose an administrator account on upgrade.

Before this commit, the default database path was derived from the database module's import.meta.url. In the esbuild single-file production bundle at dist/server/index.mjs, that resolved relative to dist/server. The commit instead resolves the database as process.cwd()/data/projectx.db. Therefore, a standalone bundled server that does not explicitly set PROJECTX_DB_PATH can select a different database after upgrading whenever its working directory is not the directory that produced the former module-relative path. There is no compatibility lookup or migration of the prior database. better-sqlite3 creates the newly selected file, initializeDatabase() installs an empty schema, and ensureDefaultAdmin() creates admin with the documented password admin123. If the server is automatically exposed through its existing reverse proxy, a remote unauthenticated attacker can log in before the operator recognizes the database switch and obtain full administrator control. The same path switch also makes the prior users, exams, and scores unavailable to the running service. Electron deployments are not affected because electron/main.cjs explicitly sets PROJECTX_DB_PATH, and source-mode launches from the repository root generally resolve to the same location; the vulnerable case is the supported standalone production bundle relying on the default path.

概要

Introduced. The parent revision already stored grading uploads without validating their type, but the recognition upload directory was not web-accessible. This commit adds preview URLs and a `sendFile` endpoint, converting the pre-existing validation weakness into a persistent same-origin XSS sink. Restrict uploads to verified image formats, generate a fixed safe extension, and serve previews with a fixed image Content-Type plus `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; alternatively force `Content-Disposition: attachment` or render transformed images from a separate origin. The preview route should also enforce authentication and the appropriate card/exam scope.

The grading upload's Multer configuration preserves the extension from the attacker-controlled original filename and applies only a size limit; it has no extension, MIME, or magic-byte validation. Both grading handlers now return a preview URL even when native recognition fails. The newly added preview route passes the resulting file directly to `res.sendFile()`, which derives the response Content-Type from that attacker-selected extension and does not force download or sandbox active content. At this revision, neither the grading upload nor preview route applies authentication or authorization. An unauthenticated attacker can obtain a card ID from the card API, upload a payload named `payload.html` in the `files` multipart field, receive the generated preview URL despite recognition failure, and induce a teacher or administrator to follow that legitimate same-origin URL. The payload then executes as HTML in the Project-X origin and can issue same-origin requests, read accessible application data, alter browser-visible state, or present credential-stealing UI. The client intentionally opens these preview URLs in a new tab; `rel="noreferrer"` prevents opener access but does not prevent the preview document itself from executing scripts.

攻击路径分析

No hard suppression applies: the impact is not self-only, the attacker is unauthenticated rather than privileged, the upload path is a normal product grading workflow, and the required victim navigation is plausible rather than unachievable. Repository code and executable HTTP evidence establish attacker-controlled input, persistent storage, inline text/html delivery, and absent route authorization. The strongest contrary fact is the 127.0.0.1 bind at index.ts:697-704, but the required threat model states that production deployments expose this loopback service through a reverse proxy or tunnel; the missing ingress artifact lowers confidence without mechanically changing the remote vector to localhost. Impact is medium because same-origin script execution can affect confidentiality, integrity, and user trust but no session-token theft, administrator takeover, or broad score corruption was proven. Likelihood is high for a reachable deployment because exploitation is unauthenticated, deterministic, and demonstrated, notwithstanding required user interaction. Applying the required matrix mechanically, medium impact multiplied by high likelihood yields medium adjusted criticality.

路径
Unauthenticated remote attacker --Uploads HTML bytes with an attacker-selected .html filename--> Public Multer grading upload --Stores bytes under a generated filename retaining .html--> Persistent recognition/uploads/<cardId> storage --Recognition result exposes a preview URL even when recognition fails--> Public res.sendFile preview route --Serves the stored bytes inline as text/html without CSP, nosniff, or attachment disposition--> Teacher or administrator browser --Attacker script executes with the Project-X origin after victim navigation--> Project-X origin APIs, data, and trusted UI

The Express answer-card service is a production grading component backed by SQLite and persistent upload storage. Its recognitionUpload configuration takes path.extname(file.originalname), so an unauthenticated request can cause attacker-controlled bytes to be stored with a .html extension. The objective and combined grading handlers expose preview URLs in both success and exception branches. The preview route then calls res.sendFile() without authentication, a fixed image media type, download disposition, CSP, or nosniff protection. The supplied executable HTTP reproduction confirmed unauthenticated card creation/listing, HTML upload, persistence across server restart, and a byte-identical preview response with Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8. The application also renders preview URLs as target=_blank links; rel=noreferrer prevents opener access but does not sandbox the loaded document. Strongest counterevidence includes the explicit 127.0.0.1 bind, the need for victim navigation, React's normal escaping, path.basename/safeId traversal controls, the existence of an unused bearer authentication middleware, and the absence of directly observed browser execution. None prevents this sink: the production threat model permits proxy exposure, React does not render the response, traversal controls do not constrain its media type, no auth middleware is attached to these routes, and standard browser behavior for the demonstrated inline HTML response is deterministic. However, the victim-interaction requirement, missing ingress artifact, and lack of proof of bearer-token theft constrain impact to medium.

发生可能性
High - For a proxy-exposed deployment, exploitation is low-complexity and requires no account: card IDs can be listed or created publicly, the upload accepts arbitrary bytes and extensions, and the server returns a usable preview URL even after recognition failure. The executable HTTP reproduction exercised the complete storage and delivery path. Victim interaction and uncertainty about actual proxy deployment are limiting factors, but a same-origin grading-preview link is credible social-engineering material and the attack does not require a race, secret, or privileged write path. | Remote network vector
影响程度
Medium - The payload executes under the trusted Project-X origin in a victim browser and can access origin-readable application responses, invoke origin-accessible operations, alter the displayed interface, and present credential-phishing content. This crosses an unauthenticated-attacker-to-teacher/admin-browser trust boundary. Impact is not high because exploitation requires victim navigation, the revision uses explicit bearer authentication rather than proven ambient privileged cookies, no bearer-token theft or administrator takeover was demonstrated, and several relevant APIs were already unauthenticated.
假设条件
The Node service is exposed to intended school users through the reverse-proxy or Cloudflare-tunnel deployment described by the supplied threat model; the repository itself contains no ingress manifest.
The frontend and grading preview are served from the same browser origin, as indicated by the relative preview URL and application route composition.
A teacher or administrator can be induced to open the legitimate Project-X preview URL, either through social engineering or while handling grading-related content.
Normal browser handling of an inline text/html response executes its script because the response has no blocking Content-Security-Policy or forced-download disposition.
A Project-X deployment reachable through its configured reverse proxy or tunnel
A valid card ID, obtainable from the unauthenticated card-list endpoint or by creating a card
A multipart upload no larger than 20 MiB whose original filename has an active extension such as .html
A teacher or administrator opening the returned or attacker-supplied preview URL
控制措施
startServer binds the Node service to 127.0.0.1, limiting direct exposure when no proxy or tunnel is configured.
Multer limits each recognition upload to 20 MiB but does not limit the content to images.
safeId and path.basename constrain directory traversal but do not prevent active-content upload or inline HTML delivery.
The client uses target=_blank with rel=noreferrer, which limits opener/referrer behavior but does not disable scripts in the preview document.
React auto-escapes JSX content, but the vulnerable document bypasses React and is served directly by Express.
Bearer authentication middleware exists elsewhere in the repository but is not attached to the affected card, grading, or preview routes.
Recognition attempts to process the file, but both success and failure branches expose the stored upload, so recognizer rejection is not a mitigation.
盲点
No reverse-proxy, Cloudflare-tunnel, Kubernetes, or load-balancer manifest exists in the checkout, so public exposure relies on the supplied production threat model rather than a concrete repository deployment artifact.
Actual JavaScript execution was not observed in a browser because the bundled Electron binary could not start without libatk-1.0.so.0; the server-side prerequisite was nevertheless demonstrated as an unsandboxed inline text/html response.
The validation environment lacked the declared bcrypt native package and used an inert seeded administrator row solely to start the application; this did not modify the affected routing or upload behavior.
No evidence proves that a privileged bearer token is stored in browser-readable storage at this revision or automatically sent by the preview document, so account takeover and authenticated administrator actions are not claimed.
Static evidence does not establish how operators distribute preview links, how often teachers open externally supplied links, or whether an external proxy adds defensive CSP, nosniff, or Content-Disposition headers.

概要

This range introduces the cancellation endpoint and its taskkill fallback. The initial liveness check correctly considers both exitCode and signalCode, but the delayed check omits signalCode and retains no cancellation handle, introducing a PID-reuse time-of-check/time-of-use flaw.

cancelScan() first terminates the scanner child with child.kill(), then unconditionally retains a two-second watchdog associated only with its numeric PID. The watchdog tests child.exitCode === null but does not test child.signalCode. In Node.js, a child terminated by a signal normally retains a null exitCode while signalCode is set, including after the close event. Consequently, the watchdog can execute taskkill /F /T even though the original scanner process has exited. Because the close handler does not cancel this watchdog, Windows may have reused the PID for another process by the time taskkill runs, causing an unrelated process tree running under the server's account to be terminated. When native scanning is enabled, a scanner API key or a user with GRADE_WRITE can reach the newly added cancel endpoint; repeated start/cancel requests can increase process churn and the likelihood of collateral termination. The fallback should be canceled on child close and should at minimum require both exitCode and signalCode to remain null before invoking taskkill, preferably with additional process-identity validation.

验证

 Demonstrate that the scanner child can close from the cancellation signal while exitCode remains null before the two-second watchdog fires.
 Demonstrate that the uncancelled production watchdog still invokes taskkill after the original child has closed.
 Verify that the forced-kill sink uses only the captured numeric PID, with no signalCode, active-child, or process-identity validation.
 Reproduce an actual Windows PID-reuse collision and collateral termination of an unrelated process tree; this was not feasible on the Linux validation host.

攻击路径分析

The calibrated impact is low because the supported effect is bounded same-host availability loss with no demonstrated data, identity, or grading-integrity compromise. Likelihood is low because the stale watchdog is proven but collateral harm depends on a short Windows PID-reuse race plus scanner enablement and authorized access. Under the required matrix, impact=low with any non-ignore likelihood yields low. Hard suppression does not apply: this is not self-only, operator-only, developer-only, or purely local correctness behavior. A scanner or grading principal is authorized to cancel the scanner child but is not thereby authorized to terminate unrelated host processes, so the issue represents a limited privilege-boundary delta in a supported production scanner workflow. The strong counterevidence—loopback binding, default-disabled web TWAIN surface, default authentication, session-state checks, and the unproven final PID collision—keeps the finding at low rather than making it non-reportable.

路径
Scanner/full API-key client or GRADE_WRITE user --uses authorized scanner endpoint when TWAIN is enabled--> POST /api/scanner/scan creates an active native scan session --supplies the returned nonterminal session ID--> POST /api/scanner/scan/:sessionId/cancel --route invokes cancelScan--> cancelScan calls child.kill() and schedules a two-second watchdog --termination signal ends the original child--> Scanner child closes with exitCode null and signalCode set --watchdog remains pending after close and holds only the numeric PID--> Windows potentially reuses the released numeric PID --watchdog checks only exitCode === null--> taskkill /F /T /PID targets the current holder of that PID --forced recursive termination under server-account authority--> Unrelated same-host process tree may be terminated

Attacker story: a holder of a scanner/full API key or a user with GRADE_WRITE starts a native scan and cancels its returned session while scanner-bridge.exe is active. The cancellation route calls cancelScan, which sends child.kill() and schedules taskkill for two seconds later. A signal-terminated Node child can have exitCode === null while signalCode is set even after close, but the watchdog checks only exitCode. The close/error handlers remove the child from activeScans without cancelling the watchdog. The supplied executable harness exercised these production functions and observed the original child close approximately 105 ms after cancellation, followed by taskkill dispatch for the now-absent PID at two seconds. If Windows reuses that PID, taskkill /F /T can terminate the replacement process tree under the server account. The strongest counterevidence is that native TWAIN is disabled by default for web deployments, Electron enables it on a loopback-bound server, default authentication requires a scanner/full key or GRADE_WRITE, and actual harm additionally depends on an unproven Windows PID-reuse collision in a short interval. Existing verification tests cover cancellation before child registration rather than this active-child watchdog, so their success does not negate the stale-PID behavior. No secret data flows through this flaw; the security effect is limited to host availability.

发生可能性
Low - The stale-PID taskkill dispatch is directly reproducible, and authorized scanner clients or GRADE_WRITE users can invoke the normal start/cancel workflow. Nevertheless, the final impact requires Windows, explicitly enabled native scanning, an active bridge, suitable authorization, signal-driven exit, and PID reuse in an approximately two-second window. The service also binds to loopback and the web deployment disables TWAIN by default. Repeated churn may increase opportunity but does not make the collision deterministic.
影响程度
Low - Successful exploitation can terminate one unrelated same-host process tree that the Project-X service account is allowed to kill. This crosses the intended boundary of cancelling only scanner-bridge.exe, but the demonstrated consequence is availability loss rather than confidentiality, grade integrity, identity compromise, or fleet-wide impact. The attacker cannot deterministically choose the replacement process, and no actual collateral termination was demonstrated.
假设条件
The affected deployment runs on Windows, where the fallback invokes taskkill.
Native TWAIN scanning is enabled through PROJECTX_ENABLE_SCANNER=1/true or PROJECTX_VARIANT=teacher-scanner.
The attacker possesses a scanner/full API key or an authenticated account with GRADE_WRITE; alternatively, the operator has explicitly disabled authentication.
A scanner session reaches the point where scanner-bridge.exe is registered in activeScans and remains live when cancellation is requested.
The original scanner child exits after child.kill(), but its numeric PID is reassigned to another process before the two-second watchdog runs.
Remote reachability requires a reverse proxy, tunnel, or comparable ingress to the loopback-bound Express service; the checkout does not establish such ingress for the scanner-enabled deployment.
Windows host
Native TWAIN scanner feature enabled
Valid scanner/full API key or authenticated GRADE_WRITE account under the default enforced-auth configuration
Active scanner-bridge child associated with a nonterminal session
Signal-driven child exit before the two-second watchdog
Numeric PID reuse during the remaining watchdog interval
An unrelated process that the Project-X OS account is permitted to terminate receives the reused PID
控制措施
Native TWAIN routes are feature-gated and disabled by default in the web package.
The server binds to 127.0.0.1; nonlocal access requires separate ingress.
Authentication is enabled by default.
Scanner routes require a scanner/full API key or GRADE_WRITE permission when authentication is enforced.
The cancellation route verifies that the session exists and is not already completed, errored, or cancelled.
cancelScan initially rejects missing or already-terminated children by checking both exitCode and signalCode.
The forced fallback waits two seconds, narrowing the PID-reuse window.
taskkill executes without a shell and receives the PID as a fixed argument, preventing command injection.
No general rate limit constrains repeated scan/start cancellation churn.
The close/error handlers remove activeScans state but do not cancel or revalidate the forced-kill watchdog.
盲点
The validation host was Linux; a real Windows taskkill execution and actual PID-reuse collision were not observed.
Repository artifacts do not establish whether a scanner-enabled deployment is exposed through a reverse proxy, tunnel, or LAN ingress.
Windows PID allocation and reuse frequency under realistic scanner workload are not established by repository evidence.
The identity and privilege level of the production Windows service account are deployment-specific and unknown.
The executable validation harness instrumented the taskkill sink and proved stale dispatch after child close, but did not prove termination of a replacement process.
No manifests in the examined checkout establish OS-level process isolation, service recovery, or endpoint rate limiting outside the application.

严重级别

概要

This commit introduces the vulnerable deployment configuration by generating and including project-x-server.service in the Ubuntu server archive. Exploitation requires the operator to install the supplied unit without separately overriding its user or filesystem permissions; that is the unit's default and expected system-level behavior.

The generated systemd unit omits User, Group, UMask, and filesystem-hardening directives. A system-level systemd service therefore runs as root with the default 0022 umask. On a clean installation, the application creates /var/lib/project-x and its subdirectories without explicit modes, and SQLite and uploaded files are consequently normally created as root-owned but world-readable directories/files (0755/0644). The database contains student records, scores, reusable initial passwords, and provider API keys, while the answer-card directory contains uploaded papers and answer images. Any unprivileged local account can therefore read these assets under the default configuration. Running the network- and upload-facing Node process as root also turns a future parser or application code-execution flaw into host-root compromise. The packaged unit should instead declare a dedicated User and Group, set UMask=0077, provision private state directories (for example with StateDirectory and StateDirectoryMode=0700), and add systemd hardening such as NoNewPrivileges and ProtectSystem.

验证
 The packaged Ubuntu artifact contains an unsafe system-level unit and deployment instructions install/use it without compensating controls. The artifact does contain the unsafe unit, but its generated README documents foreground ./start.sh and does not provide systemd installation instructions.
 Under systemd/default process semantics, the unit runs as root with umask 0022, while application state is created without restrictive explicit modes; this was confirmed by systemd-analyze and source tracing.
 A focused realistic reproduction shows the resulting database and answer-card paths are traversable and sensitive files readable by an unrelated unprivileged local UID.
 Repository and dynamic evidence confirm that exposed storage contains student identity, reusable initial passwords, provider API keys, and uploaded assets, with no startup chmod, ACL, or encryption control preventing disclosure at this commit.
 Preconditions and impact are bounded to operators who install the supplied unit without overrides; root execution is treated as impact amplification rather than a demonstrated standalone RCE.

攻击路径分析

The original medium rating is reduced after separating impact from reachability. Impact is high because a successful local read exposes installation-wide educational records, reusable initial passwords, provider credentials, and uploaded images. Likelihood is low because network scope is none and exploitation requires both optional systemd-unit installation and an unrelated lower-privileged local account; the package README instead documents foreground startup and supplies no evidence that untrusted users receive server shell access. The executable PoC proves the permissions and disclosure once those plausible conditions hold, so the issue is not ignored as unachievable or self-only. Applying the required matrix mechanically, high impact multiplied by low likelihood yields low severity. No additional hard suppression applies because the attacker need not be root, operator, developer, or the owner of the disclosed records.

路径
Packaged systemd unit installed system-wide --Unit has no User, Group, or UMask directive--> Node service runs as root with default 0022 umask --Root process initializes SQLite and answer-card storage--> Application creates /var/lib/project-x state without explicit modes --Inherited modes make state world-readable--> Unprivileged local account reads 0755 directories and 0644 files --Direct filesystem and SQLite reads bypass application authentication--> Sensitive school records, credentials, API keys, and uploaded images disclosed

The Ubuntu package generator includes a systemd unit for the production web server. The unit starts Node from /opt, points sensitive SQLite and answer-card state at /var/lib/project-x, but declares no User, Group, UMask, StateDirectory, NoNewPrivileges, or filesystem protection. System services consequently run as root unless overridden. Application initialization creates the database parent and answer-card directories without explicit modes, and the upload path does the same for per-card directories. Under the ordinary 0022 mask, clean-install directories and files become 0755 and 0644. Application authentication and loopback binding do not protect direct local filesystem reads. The supplied executable validation reproduced root-owned modes and successfully read a student initial password, provider key, and uploaded asset as the unrelated nobody UID. The strongest counterevidence is deployment prevalence: the generated README instructs users to run ./start.sh in the foreground and never instructs them to install the bundled unit. It also does not establish untrusted local accounts on production hosts. Therefore the direct confidentiality impact is high when reached, but the repository-supported likelihood is low. The calibrated and policy-adjusted severity is low rather than the original medium.

发生可能性
Low - The unsafe unit is genuinely shipped and normal systemd semantics make exploitation straightforward once it is enabled, as confirmed by the supplied executable validation. However, the attack is not network-reachable: it requires a distinct unprivileged local account, installation of an optional unit that the README does not tell operators to install, use of its SQLite paths, and absence of secure overrides or private pre-provisioning. The repository does not establish that school server hosts normally expose local accounts to untrusted users. These constraints make likelihood low but not unachievable.
影响程度
High - Successful exploitation permits broad read access to the service's SQLite database and uploaded answer-card state. Repository evidence shows the database contains student identity information, scores and rankings, reusable plaintext initial passwords, and plaintext provider API keys. Uploaded papers or answer images can also be read. This is a high confidentiality impact across the installation. Unprivileged modification was not demonstrated, and root-process compromise is not counted because the repository evidence does not establish a code-execution primitive.
假设条件
An operator installs and enables the packaged project-x-server.service as a system-level unit without adding a User, Group, UMask, ACL, or other override.
The service uses the unit's SQLite configuration and fixed /var/lib/project-x state paths.
The state directory is created on a clean installation rather than being pre-provisioned with restrictive modes.
The host has an unrelated lower-privileged local account capable of ordinary filesystem reads.
The systemd manager uses the normal root service identity and default 0022 file-creation mask in the absence of explicit directives.
Installation and activation of the supplied systemd unit
No secure systemd override or pre-provisioned private state directory
SQLite-backed operation using the unit's configured paths
Access to an unprivileged local OS account on the server
控制措施
PROJECTX_AUTH_ENFORCE=1 is set in the unit, but application authentication is bypassed by direct filesystem reads.
The server binds to loopback at 127.0.0.1:5174, reducing direct network exposure of the Node listener.
Root ownership prevents the demonstrated unprivileged account from modifying the files under ordinary DAC; the proven direct effect is confidentiality loss.
The README's foreground start workflow can be safe if an operator deliberately launches it as a dedicated unprivileged account with a restrictive umask and private state paths.
No User, Group, UMask, StateDirectory, StateDirectoryMode, NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem, or equivalent service hardening is present in the packaged unit.
No compensating chmod or application-level umask for the affected state was identified in the relevant repository paths.
盲点
The repository contains no host-account provisioning or SSH policy, so the prevalence of unrelated unprivileged local users on deployed school servers is unknown.
The repository does not contain an Nginx or tunnel deployment manifest proving whether the loopback service is publicly exposed; this does not affect the direct local-filesystem vector.
The README does not describe how or whether operators install the included systemd unit, so affected deployment prevalence is unknown.
Existing installations may have operator-supplied ACLs, secure unit overrides, private parent-directory modes, or a global systemd DefaultUMask that prevent disclosure.
The dynamic validation reproduced systemd-equivalent UID and umask behavior rather than launching the unit under a live systemd PID 1.
No independent application, upload-parser, or native-parser code-execution primitive was established, so host-root compromise remains an unscored amplification concern.

Previously, the response exposed only the numeric scan record ID; the commit newly returns `scan_records.file_path` without reducing it to a basename. The normal grading flow stores Multer's `file.path` in `scan_records.file_path`; the upload destination is derived from the absolute `dataDir`. Although a teacher is an authenticated application user, the teacher is an explicitly modeled partially trusted attacker and is not authorized merely by exam:read to receive host filesystem layout; the server-to-client confidentiality boundary crossing is the vulnerability itself. The strongest counterevidence—loopback binding, production RBAC, and basename-based image resolution—reduces exposure or bounds impact but does not eliminate the verified response disclosure. 概要

This commit introduced the vulnerability by adding and mounting two sponsor GET endpoints without mandatory authentication. The existing optional authentication middleware does not reject anonymous requests, and no later authorization gate applies to these routes.

The application applies only optionalAuth before mounting /api/sponsor. That middleware always continues when no token is supplied, and the sponsor router does not install authMiddleware or check req.user. The route is also mounted before the permission gateways, none of which cover /api/sponsor. Consequently, an Internet user can directly request GET /api/sponsor to enumerate enabled payment channels and then GET /api/sponsor/qr/:channelId to retrieve a configured payment QR code, even when PROJECTX_AUTH_ENFORCE is enabled. This conflicts with the documented policy that the feature is for logged-in students, teachers, and administrators, while the frontend login check provides no protection against direct API requests. The current committed configuration contains no QR files, but deployments are explicitly expected to enable them through runtime configuration. This can disclose payment-account metadata or payee identity encoded in deployed QR codes and permits unauthenticated scraping or hotlinking. The impact is limited because no academic records, credentials, or mutable operations are exposed. The router should require authMiddleware; because image elements cannot set a bearer header, the client can fetch the image through authFetch and display a blob URL.

The established facts produce low impact and high likelihood. Applying the required matrix mechanically, impact=low with any non-ignore likelihood yields low severity. Hard suppression does not apply: the impact is not self-only; the attacker needs no operator, developer, local, physical, or authenticated privilege; and the documented operator act of enabling a payment QR is ordinary population of application data rather than a privilege the attacker must obtain. The route is part of a real runtime product workflow, and the supplied production threat model provides a realistic remote path through a proxy or tunnel. Conversely, escalation above low is unwarranted because the stock checkout contains no QR image, the endpoint is read-only, path confinement blocks arbitrary file reads, and the potentially disclosed payment material is intended for all logged-in users. Final decision: reportable as a low-severity authentication-control regression, not ignored.

路径
Unauthenticated Internet attacker --Sends anonymous HTTP GET requests--> Deployment reverse proxy or Cloudflare tunnel --Forwards public deployment traffic to the loopback service--> Express API on loopback port 5174 --Routes /api traffic through optional identity parsing--> optionalAuth middleware --Continues without req.user when no token is supplied--> GET /api/sponsor --Returns enabled channel IDs and QR URLs--> GET /api/sponsor/qr/:channelId --Reads the configured fixed-directory image and returns it with res.sendFile--> Operator-configured sponsor metadata and QR file

Project-X's Express service mounts optionalAuth for every /api request and then mounts sponsorRoutes without authMiddleware. optionalAuth expressly permits requests without tokens, while the later RBAC gateways do not cover /api/sponsor. The metadata handler reveals enabled channel IDs, names, descriptions, and QR URLs; the QR handler uses an enabled channel to return the configured image with res.sendFile. The supplied executable validation started the real application with PROJECTX_AUTH_ENFORCE=1: anonymous /api/cards was rejected with 401, while anonymous /api/sponsor and /api/sponsor/qr/validation returned 200, and the returned PNG matched the configured fixture byte-for-byte. This is a genuine missing-authentication vulnerability in a product workflow, not merely a frontend correctness issue, because direct API requests bypass the UI's logged-in-user gate. Counterevidence materially limits severity: the server binds to loopback, the stock sponsor configuration has qrFile set to null, filenames are confined to the sponsor QR directory, and the disclosed content is intended for all authenticated users rather than a narrow privileged audience. It remains reportable at low severity because documented production exposure and documented runtime QR enablement make the anonymous trust-boundary crossing realistic.

发生可能性
High - For a deployment exposed through the production reverse proxy or tunnel, exploitation requires only two ordinary GET requests, no authentication, no user interaction, and no complex guessing because the metadata endpoint enumerates channel IDs. The executable validation confirmed the complete path while enforced RBAC blocked a protected control route. An actual QR disclosure depends on documented operator configuration, and direct service binding is loopback-only, but both conditions are plausible normal deployment states rather than attacker-held privileges. Likelihood is therefore high within an exposed, QR-enabled deployment. | Remote network vector
影响程度
Low - The maximum demonstrated effect is read-only disclosure of enabled sponsor metadata and a deployment-configured payment QR, potentially including payee or payment-account identity encoded in the image. The route exposes no credentials, academic records, arbitrary filesystem content, executable sink, or state-changing operation. The material is also intended for broad distribution to every authenticated role. Impact is therefore low.
假设条件
The deployment follows the supplied production threat model and makes the loopback-bound Express service reachable through a reverse proxy or Cloudflare tunnel.
An operator may enable the documented sponsor feature by assigning an enabled channel a QR filename and placing the corresponding image under data/sponsor/qr/.
The documentation's statement that the feature applies to logged-in students, teachers, and administrators represents the intended access policy despite the validation checklist showing a bare local curl command.
The Express API must be reachable by the attacker, normally through the deployment reverse proxy or tunnel described in the supplied threat model.
Disclosure of an actual payment QR requires an enabled sponsor channel with qrFile configured and the referenced file present under data/sponsor/qr/.
No account, bearer token, cookie, user interaction, or privileged attacker action is required.
控制措施
PROJECTX_AUTH_ENFORCE enables RBAC gates for selected business-route prefixes, but no such gate covers /api/sponsor.
authMiddleware can enforce a valid bearer or query token, but sponsorRoutes does not use it.
optionalAuth parses a supplied token but deliberately permits anonymous requests.
The frontend hides the application and account menu until a user is present, but this is not a server-side authorization control.
Only channels marked enabled are returned or served.
A QR response requires a configured qrFile and an existing file.
path.basename and the fixed data/sponsor/qr directory prevent the channel configuration from serving arbitrary paths.
The service directly listens on 127.0.0.1, reducing exposure unless deployment ingress forwards traffic to it.
There is no route-specific rate limit preventing anonymous enumeration, scraping, or hotlinking.
盲点
The repository does not contain a concrete reverse-proxy, Cloudflare tunnel, load-balancer, or firewall manifest establishing the exact exposure of every deployment.
The committed checkout contains no real payment QR, so the confidentiality of production QR contents and any encoded payee identifiers cannot be measured statically.
The bare local curl in the sponsor validation checklist creates unresolved intent ambiguity even though the same documentation limits the feature audience to logged-in users.
No production cache, CDN, proxy logging, or hotlink-protection configuration is available to determine whether anonymous QR responses could be retained or redistributed beyond the application.
The executable PoC used a startup-only bcrypt shim because the checkout's installed dependencies omitted bcrypt; the tested anonymous handlers and protected control did not exercise bcrypt.

Automatically creates an active administrator with the hard-coded `admin123` password on every database that lacks an `admin` row.

概要

This commit introduces the vulnerability by adding automatic creation of a fixed-password administrator and mounting the corresponding network login endpoint. Replace the fixed password with a cryptographically random per-installation bootstrap secret delivered through a protected channel, and require a one-time password change before issuing a fully privileged session.

Every fresh database is initialized with an active `admin` account whose password is deterministically set to `admin123`. The server creates this account before listening and then publicly mounts `/api/auth/login`; submitting the known credentials returns a valid eight-hour bearer token associated with the wildcard administrator role. This revision has no first-run secret randomization, `must_change_password` state, password-change route, or forced-change check, so the credential remains usable until an operator modifies the database through some out-of-band mechanism. Because the loopback server may be exposed through the documented reverse-proxy or tunnel deployment, an unauthenticated network attacker can claim the bootstrap administrator account on a fresh or restored installation before the legitimate operator secures it.

 The created account is assigned the administrator role whose stored permissions are ["*"].

攻击路径分析

The original critical rating assumed both Internet reachability and an immediately usable wildcard administrator session. Repository evidence confirms the fixed credential and successful admin-token issuance, but contradicts both severity-driving assumptions: src/apps/answer-card/server/index.ts:446-455 restricts direct exposure to localhost, and no checked-in ingress exists; src/server/middleware/auth.ts:28-73 defines authorization controls that are never mounted, so the token has no demonstrated privileged consumer. The issue is retained rather than suppressed because the public login route is a real product workflow, the unauthenticated-to-admin identity boundary is verified by executable evidence, and operator forwarding remains plausible under the supplied threat model. Applying the required matrix mechanically, low impact combined with low likelihood yields low adjusted criticality.

路径
Unauthenticated caller with local or forwarded access --submits the known bootstrap identifier and password--> POST /api/auth/login --looks up the active account and verifies its bcrypt hash--> Active fixed-credential admin row created on a fresh database --returns an opaque token and admin identity--> Eight-hour role-1 administrator bearer token --attack chain stops because no mounted privileged route authenticates this token--> Privileged token-consuming API not present or mounted in this revision

Attacker story: when Project-X starts with a database lacking an admin row, it creates an active role-1 administrator using a deterministic credential that is also disclosed in repository documentation and startup logging. An unauthenticated caller who can reach the service can submit that credential to the publicly mounted login route. Password verification then produces a random bearer token valid for eight hours and returns an admin user object. The executable validation reproduced this identity transition. The strongest counterevidence is that the exact server listens only on 127.0.0.1, the README documents only local use, and no proxy, tunnel, ingress, or load balancer is checked in. More importantly, authMiddleware and requireRole are merely defined: they are not mounted on the application routes, and /api/auth/me itself returns 401 because req.user is never populated. Consequently, the token does not provide a demonstrated capability beyond the admin-labelled session in this revision; card and scanner routes are independently unauthenticated rather than unlocked by this token. These facts are dispositive against the original critical account-takeover impact, but not against the existence of a fixed bootstrap-credential vulnerability in a real product authentication workflow.

发生可能性
Low - Use of the credential is trivial and was reproduced, and a fresh installation naturally satisfies the missing-admin-row condition. Nevertheless, repository artifacts bind the service to loopback, use an ephemeral loopback port in Electron, document only local URLs, and provide no public ingress. Remote exploitation depends on external operator forwarding described by the supplied threat model but not evidenced at this commit. This makes likelihood low for the repository-default deployment.
影响程度
Low - The unauthenticated-to-admin identity transition is proven, but the only demonstrated effects are issuance of an admin-labelled in-memory token, disclosure of the non-password user object, and update of last-login state. No mounted endpoint was found that uses the token to expose protected data or perform administrator operations, and /api/auth/me does not authenticate successfully because its router lacks authMiddleware. Counting the independently unauthenticated card and scanner routes as consequences of this token would invent an unsupported chain. Realized impact at this commit is therefore low.
假设条件
The attacker acts while the server is running against a fresh or restored database that has no existing admin row.
Remote exploitation requires an operator-supplied reverse proxy, tunnel, or equivalent forwarding because this revision binds the server to 127.0.0.1 and contains no ingress or load-balancer configuration.
The supplied threat model's reverse-proxy or tunnel deployment is plausible, but it is not documented or implemented by artifacts at this exact commit.
The validation PoC substituted bcryptjs for the unavailable native bcrypt package; database initialization, routing, credential selection, role assignment, and token generation remained repository code.
The application is running.
The database lacks a user whose username is admin.
The attacker can reach the loopback listener locally or through operator-configured forwarding.
The default administrator credential has not been replaced through an out-of-band database operation.
控制措施
Passwords are stored using bcrypt with cost 10 rather than plaintext in the database.
Unknown users and incorrect passwords receive the same generic authentication error.
User lookup requires is_active = 1.
Default-admin creation stops if an admin row already exists.
Session tokens are generated from 32 random bytes and expire after eight hours.
The production entry point binds directly to 127.0.0.1.
Electron launches the server on an ephemeral loopback port with context isolation, Node integration disabled, and sandboxing enabled.
No login rate limit is implemented.
No persistent forced-password-change control is implemented.
Authentication and role middleware are not mounted on privileged product routes in this revision.
盲点
A reverse proxy or tunnel may exist outside the checkout; no deployment manifests establish or exclude such forwarding.
No protected downstream service consuming this token is present in the inspected revision; an external component sharing the in-memory token store would be unlikely but cannot be evaluated from absent artifacts.
The validation runtime used bcryptjs because the checkout lacked the declared native bcrypt binary, although the relevant API and hash behavior were compatible.
Static repository analysis cannot determine whether operators manually replace the bootstrap credential in deployed database files before exposing the service.
The broader absence of authentication on card and scanner routes is a separate issue and was not attributed to this fixed-credential attack path.

comments: The normal-operation decision assumes `serverSkin` reflects the current persisted value, although ScannerApp continues supplying the stale login snapshot.
Every change is compared against `user.themeSkin`, but the fire-and-forget PATCH never updates that value; reverting to the login-time skin is therefore incorrectly skipped.

严重级别
Informational

调整 以提高未来扫描的准确性

提交

操作者：火箭

代码仓库
Dalian-No-5-Middle-School-I-T-C/Project-X
举报
聊天
概要

Introduced: the commit adds post-login skin controls without keeping the comparison baseline synchronized after PATCH requests. This causes recoverable account-preference inconsistency but does not cross an authorization boundary or affect sensitive examination data.

After login, `serverSkin` is derived from `user.themeSkin`, but a successful settings PATCH does not update or refresh that user object. For example, if the account initially uses `paper-edge`, selecting `flat` sends a PATCH and changes the database to `flat`. Selecting `paper-edge` again is then compared with the stale login-time `user.themeSkin === "paper-edge"`; `skinPatchDecision` returns `patch: false`, leaving the database at `flat` even though the UI and local storage show `paper-edge`. After logout or on another device, the supposedly reverted preference restores as `flat`. The exact range makes this reachable through the newly added post-login switchers. Track the last successfully requested/persisted skin, update the authenticated user after a successful PATCH, or refresh settings rather than always comparing against the immutable login snapshot.

验证
 Confirm that authenticated scanner pages expose controlled post-login skin changes through onSkinChange={setSkin}.
 Confirm that ScannerApp compares against the login-time user.themeSkin and neither mutates nor refreshes that object after a successful PATCH.

 Exercise the authenticated production settings endpoint and verify that the first change persists while the suppressed revert leaves the database inconsistent with visible/local state.
 Establish preconditions and impact scope, including that only the authenticated user's cosmetic preference is affected and no security trust boundary is crossed.

攻击路径分析

Pre-policy calibration is low: mechanically, low impact remains low even with high trigger likelihood. The separate final policy pass then applies the mandatory self-only-impact suppression. Repository evidence shows that the server uses req.user.id at src/apps/answer-card/server/index.ts:774-784, validates themeSkin at lines 807-814, and updates only that same user's cosmetic fields at lines 831-835. No realistic lower-privileged attacker can affect another identity, sensitive examination data, authorization state, or service availability. The issue is therefore a confirmed correctness bug but is not security-reportable and is adjusted to ignore.

路径
Ordinary authenticated scanner user --selects alternate skin and later selects original skin--> Post-login SkinSwitcher --records explicit selection and calls onSkinChange--> ScannerApp skin state and session/local storage --effect compares current skin with stale authenticated-user snapshot--> skinPatchDecision using login-time user.themeSkin --allows first change but suppresses return to login-time value--> Authenticated PATCH /api/users/me/settings --first request updates only req.user.id using validated enum values--> Same user's theme_skin and ui_style database fields --database remains at intermediate skin--> Visible/local preference diverges from persisted preference

Attacker story: an ordinary authenticated user selects the alternate scanner skin and then selects the original login-time skin. The controlled switcher makes both actions reachable in normal product use. ScannerApp persists the first change, but its fire-and-forget request neither updates nor refreshes the authenticated user object. The next decision still compares against the login-time user.themeSkin, so the return to that value is incorrectly treated as already persisted and no request is sent. Executable validation against the production guard and authenticated Express route confirmed that the browser-visible value became paper-edge while the database remained flat. The strongest repository counterevidence is the server-side control at index.ts:774-814: authentication is required, the target is derived exclusively from req.user.id, and themeSkin is restricted to two non-executable values. This is dispositive against cross-user modification, authorization bypass, secret exposure, code execution, and examination-integrity impact, although it does not disprove the functional inconsistency. The existing verification script is counterevidence against simpler login-transition regressions, but it permits only one post-login switch and is therefore not dispositive against the demonstrated two-switch sequence.

发生可能性
High - The functional defect is easy to trigger through normal authenticated UI actions: select the alternate skin and then return to the login-time skin before refreshing the user context. The supplied executable PoC reproduced the state divergence through the production guard and authenticated settings endpoint. This high correctness-trigger likelihood does not create an attacker advantage.
影响程度
Low - The demonstrated effect is limited to a recoverable inconsistency in the initiating user's cosmetic theme preference. There is no cross-user write, privilege escalation, sensitive-data disclosure, examination-integrity change, code execution, or meaningful availability loss.
假设条件
Production authentication remains enabled as required by the supplied threat model.
The scanner web client can be exposed through the operator-managed reverse proxy or tunnel described by the supplied threat model, although no concrete ingress manifest is present in the checkout.
The first skin PATCH succeeds and the authenticated user context is not refreshed before the user selects the original login-time skin.
The attacker story concerns an ordinary authenticated user manipulating only that same user's theme preference.
A valid authenticated user session
The account's login-time skin is one of the two supported values
The user selects the other skin and the resulting PATCH succeeds
Without refreshing the authenticated user object, the same user selects the original login-time skin
控制措施
authMiddleware requires a valid session when PROJECTX_AUTH_ENFORCE is enabled.
requirePasswordChangeCompleted blocks ordinary API use until mandatory initial password replacement is complete.
The PATCH target is taken from req.user.id; the request cannot select another user's ID.
themeSkin accepts only flat or paper-edge and maps to fixed ui_style values.
The sink is a parameterized database update with no executable interpretation.
CORS uses an origin allowlist and credentials are not exposed through a wildcard origin.
The Node service binds to 127.0.0.1; remote access depends on operator-managed ingress.
The settings mutation affects only cosmetic account fields and does not touch grades, scans, exams, permissions, credentials, or publication state.
盲点
No concrete reverse-proxy, load-balancer, or Cloudflare tunnel manifest is present in the checkout; remote exposure is based on the supplied threat model and the server's reverse-proxy-aware configuration.
The supplied PoC did not execute a full browser automation click-through, although it exercised the production decision function and authenticated production HTTP endpoint.
Deployment-specific modifications to authentication, frontend routing, or user-context refresh behavior outside this commit could change reachability, but none are evidenced in the repository.
Static repository analysis cannot verify the operator's actual PROJECTX_AUTH_ENFORCE, CORS, proxy, or HTTPS settings.

概要

Introduced. At the baseline revision, the plain INSERT raised a uniqueness error when a fixed demo card ID was already occupied, preventing the importer from touching that card. The new INSERT OR IGNORE suppresses the conflict and allows all subsequent seed operations to treat the pre-existing card as the demo card. The importer should check the insert result and only reuse an existing row after verifying is_demo = 1 and the expected demo identity; otherwise it should abort or allocate a collision-free card ID.

The demo importer uses fixed card IDs such as 88000001 and 88000002. This commit changed answer-card creation from INSERT to INSERT OR IGNORE but does not verify that an ignored row is actually demo-owned. If a production card already has one of those IDs, seedExam continues using that real card as the card for a demo exam. For cards with question data, ensureDemoObjectiveBlock then inserts a demo objective block and hard-coded answer keys into the existing card. For card 88000001, seedFillBlankDemo similarly inserts a demo subjective block, questions, and an image asset. The stale comment in seedFillBlankDemo still states that an occupied demo ID will make seedExam fail, but INSERT OR IGNORE now suppresses that failure. Cleanup only deletes answer_cards where is_demo = 1, so a colliding real card and the injected blocks can survive demo cleanup. This can silently alter the layout or answer metadata used by real examinations and subsequent grading. The operation requires an administrator with SYSTEM_MANAGE to invoke demo import, so this is primarily an integrity and administrative-safety defect rather than a privilege-boundary vulnerability.

In particular, the new teacher is left without a fine-grained teacher role, which activates the application's backward-compatibility path granting visibility to all exams and combines with the teacher role's write permissions.

The commit introduces the string `indeterminate` in two places even though `ObjectiveMode` defines the value as `indefinite`. The comparison in the question-type change handler therefore produces TypeScript error TS2367, preventing the repository's normal `npm run build` workflow because it runs `tsc --noEmit`. If type checking is bypassed, selecting the valid `indefinite` mode makes both comparisons at line 2382 true and deletes every question's `scoringRule`. The grading implementation relies on that rule to award partial credit, so subsequent grading can silently award zero or fallback scores across all affected questions and students. Introduced. The commit exposes and consumes a new option-layout field without implementing its end-to-end normalization and database persistence.

The final policy pass applies hard suppression: the realistic trigger is an authorized or local card-write operation, and the actor gains no privilege or cross-boundary capability beyond their existing ability to rewrite the card. 概要

This commit introduced the signing regression by changing the default-enabled electron-builder behavior to `signAndEditExecutable: false`. The icon path change uses a repository-controlled PNG and does not expose attacker input. Adding `--use-system-ca` affects only the operator-run MSI build process and is not independently exploitable under the stated trusted-build-host assumptions.

The new global Windows build option sets `signAndEditExecutable` to `false`. Electron-builder normally uses this stage to edit and Authenticode-sign the packaged application executable when signing credentials are supplied. Consequently, even a release environment configured with signing credentials will produce an unsigned inner application executable for both the portable and MSI packaging flows. This does not necessarily prevent the outer MSI or portable container from being signed independently, but it removes executable-level publisher authentication and prevents signature-enforcement policies from validating the installed or extracted application. An attacker who can modify a shared deployment copy, extracted portable application, or installed executable could substitute code without invalidating an application-executable signature. Exploitation still requires write access to a distribution or application location and subsequent user execution, so this is a low-priority supply-chain/local integrity weakness rather than a remotely reachable application vulnerability. Remove the option or set it to `true`, provide signing credentials in the release environment, and verify signatures on produced artifacts.

The calibrated gross impact is high because a successfully substituted executable can run arbitrary code and access locally stored examination data, but likelihood is low, yielding low severity under the required high-impact/low-likelihood matrix. The separate policy-adjustment pass then applies hard suppression: every supported attack path requires pre-existing privileged or protected-path write access to a build output, deployment copy, extracted portable directory, or installation directory. The disabled signature does not provide that access or a privilege-escalation delta, and there is no evidenced remote or lower-privileged product entry point. This is a genuine executable-integrity regression in a documented Windows product workflow. package.json globally sets build.win.signAndEditExecutable=false, and the supplied executable validation against pinned app-builder-lib 26.15.2 demonstrated that WinPackager.signApp returns before editing or signing the application executable even when signing would otherwise occur. The setting applies to both documented portable and MSI build commands. The strongest counterevidence is that the repository contains no signing credentials, forceCodeSigning configuration, release automation, updater, or signed artifact proving that Project-X currently operates a signed release pipeline. In addition, outer MSI or portable containers can still be signed independently, and the MSI is configured per-user. Those points do not disprove the configuration defect: valid external credentials would still be bypassed for the inner executable. They are nevertheless dispositive for reportability because exploitation requires pre-existing write authority over a protected distribution or application path, bypass or expiration of outer-container protection, and subsequent victim execution. The repository provides no remote, student, teacher, or other lower-privileged path to gain that write access. The issue therefore weakens defense-in-depth publisher authentication but does not itself cross a privilege boundary.

发生可能性
Low - There is no network-reachable signing sink, update mechanism, or repository-supported lower-privileged route to replace the executable. An attacker must already control a release share or writable application location, avoid or outlive outer-artifact verification, and induce user execution. No committed signing credentials or signed release pipeline establish that executable signing would otherwise occur. These conditions make exploitation unlikely.
影响程度
High - Successful substitution and execution provides arbitrary code execution with the victim application's user privileges. The packaged application points to a local database and answer-card data under Electron's userData directory, while project documentation states that scan images and scores are stored locally. Confidentiality, integrity, and availability consequences could therefore be high after exploitation, although the signing setting does not itself grant the necessary write access.
假设条件
Windows releases are built through the repository's electron:dist or electron:msi scripts and consume the global build.win configuration.
The pinned electron-builder/app-builder-lib 26.15.2 behavior demonstrated by the supplied validation remains representative of release builds.
A meaningful attack requires a victim to obtain or run an executable from a location the attacker can modify.
Signing credentials may be supplied outside the repository; no credentials or signed artifacts are committed.
A Windows portable or MSI release is produced using the affected electron-builder configuration.
The release environment would otherwise have valid Project-X signing credentials.
The attacker obtains write access to a shared deployment copy, extracted portable directory, or installed application executable.
Any outer-container signature check is bypassed, omitted, or no longer applicable because substitution occurs after extraction or installation.
A victim executes the substituted application.
控制措施
ASAR packaging is enabled for application resources, but it does not authenticate or protect a replaced outer application executable.
The outer MSI or portable container can be signed independently; that can detect pre-extraction tampering when signature verification is enforced.
MSI perMachine=false configures a per-user installation rather than a privileged machine-wide installation.
Electron uses contextIsolation=true, nodeIntegration=false, and sandbox=true, but those renderer controls do not mitigate whole-executable replacement.
No automatic-update mechanism was found in the repository, eliminating an evidenced remote update-delivery path for the replacement.
Filesystem and release-channel ACLs are the primary prerequisite control, but their deployment configuration is outside the repository.
盲点
No complete Windows artifact was produced in the Linux validation environment, so the actual signatures of released PE files were not directly inspected.
The repository contains no signing credentials, release CI configuration, or signed artifacts, so current operational signing practices are unknown.
External GitHub organization controls, release-asset protections, school deployment shares, Windows ACLs, AppLocker or WDAC policy, and endpoint protection are outside the repository.
The repository does not establish how many systems consume a given artifact, so fleet reach remains unknown.
An upstream Electron vendor signature might remain on some input PE files, but it would not authenticate Project-X as the publisher.

Introduced: the range adds the custom LoadLibraryA-based DSM resolver and its unsafe candidate ordering. The baseline called DSM_Entry directly and did not contain this explicit developer-path and bare-name runtime loading logic.

The commit replaces the previously linked DSM_Entry call with a custom loader. On its first TWAIN operation, it passes several unverified candidates to LoadLibraryA, including a fixed D:\ developer path followed by the bare names TWAINDSM.dll and twain_32.dll. The fixed path is checked before the packaged DLL name, while bare-name loading can include the application directory and other process search locations. LoadLibraryA executes a DLL's initialization code before GetProcAddress checks whether DSM_Entry exists, so merely planting a DLL in an applicable location is sufficient. The build script normally copies TWAINDSM.dll beside scanner-bridge.exe, which limits the bare-name case, but packaging continues with only a warning when that copy is absent and the runtime loader still prefers the hard-coded D:\ path. A lower-privileged local user who can create or replace a DLL at that path, or in an effective search directory on an installation without the bundled DLL, can obtain code execution as the account running Project-X when scanner source enumeration or scanning starts. Internet-only attackers cannot create such a local file, and managed scanner workstations are an explicit assumption, so the project-specific criticality is low. The bridge should instead resolve an operator-configured or packaged DLL to a canonical absolute path, restrict loading with LoadLibraryEx search flags, and preferably validate its publisher or digest.

攻击路径分析

Before policy suppression, conditional native code execution has high impact but low likelihood, which mechanically maps to low severity. The separate final policy pass suppresses the finding to ignore because repository evidence does not establish a realistic lower-privileged in-scope attacker who can write the hard-coded or effective search path while gaining access beyond their existing account. The documented product deployment is a loopback-only Electron scanner application running with the launching user's token, and no service elevation or cross-user ACL condition is shown. The managed-workstation assumption further weakens the local attacker story. The packaged adjacent DSM is not dispositive against the code defect because the hard-coded D: path is attempted first and packaging tolerates a missing DSM, but those facts alone do not establish the privilege-escalation delta required to make this local file-planting issue reportable under the supplied policy.

路径
Lower-privileged local Windows user --requires filesystem write access--> Attacker-controlled DLL at selected candidate path --selected before or through bare-name fallback--> LoadLibraryA candidate loop --LoadLibraryA runs DLL initialization before GetProcAddress--> scanner-bridge.exe process --inherits the launching process account token--> Native code execution with Scanner Bridge account access

This is a genuine conditional DLL-hijacking vulnerability in a production scanner workflow. native/ScannerBridge/scanner-bridge/twain_controller.cpp:40-60 loads an environment-selected path, a fixed D: developer path, TWAINDSM.dll, and twain_32.dll with LoadLibraryA. The fixed D: path is attempted before the packaged DLL name, and the two final candidates use unrestricted bare-name resolution. Because LoadLibraryA initializes the module before GetProcAddress checks for DSM_Entry, a planted DLL can execute even without exporting the expected function. Normal source enumeration reaches the sink through main.cpp:31-41, listSources at twain_controller.cpp:180-184, and openDSM at lines 400-405. The loopback GET /api/scanner/sources route also invokes scanner-bridge with the list argument, while scanning reaches the same loader. The strongest counterevidence is operational: Electron binds the API to 127.0.0.1, the build usually places a legitimate TWAINDSM.dll next to the bridge, managed scanner workstations are assumed, and the repository proves neither attacker-writable ACLs on D: nor an elevated or separate Scanner Bridge account. The adjacent DLL does not neutralize the earlier hard-coded candidate, and a failed DSM copy is only a warning, but no realistic cross-account privilege boundary is established. No executable Windows proof was run because the supplied environment lacks the required Windows runtime and toolchain.

发生可能性
Low - Exploitation is local and conditional. It requires a Windows deployment, write access to a candidate DLL path, no earlier valid DSM candidate, and a later list or scan operation. The API is loopback-only, scanner workstations are assumed managed, and the build usually packages an adjacent DSM. The hard-coded D: candidate is still tried first and packaging can continue without a DSM, but repository artifacts do not establish production ACLs, the existence or writability of D:, or an elevated Scanner Bridge identity. These conditions support low technical likelihood rather than a realistic remote or local-network attack path.
影响程度
High - If a lower-privileged attacker controls the selected DLL path and the bridge runs under a more privileged or data-rich account, DLL initialization provides arbitrary native code execution with that account's access, affecting confidentiality, integrity, and availability of local scanner operations and accessible application data. Impact is therefore high on successful cross-account exploitation, but the repository does not prove that such a privilege difference exists.
假设条件
The affected deployment is Windows and includes scanner-bridge.exe.
A lower-privileged local attacker can create or replace a DLL at the hard-coded D:\twain-dsm-2.5.1\twain-dsm-2.5.1\Releases\dsm_020403\windows\64\TWAINDSM.dll path, or at an effective Windows bare-name DLL search location.
No valid TWAIN_DSM_DLL environment candidate is selected before the attacker-controlled candidate.
A user or local request subsequently invokes scanner source enumeration or scanning.
A meaningful privilege or data-access difference exists between the file-planting attacker and the account running Project-X; the repository does not establish this difference.
Windows scanner workstation
Write access to the hard-coded D: candidate or another effective DLL search directory
Absence of an earlier valid environment-selected DSM
Invocation of scanner source enumeration or scanning
A privilege or data-access difference between attacker and Scanner Bridge account for security impact beyond self-execution
控制措施
The application server binds to 127.0.0.1 rather than a public interface.
Electron starts the local server on an ephemeral port.
The build normally copies TWAINDSM.dll beside scanner-bridge.exe, reducing the practical bare-name TWAINDSM.dll case.
The bridge executable is spawned with an argument array rather than through a command shell.
The scanner bridge runs with the launching account's token; no intentional elevation is evidenced.
Scanner workstations are assumed physically managed by the supplied threat model.
No SetDefaultDllDirectories, AddDllDirectory, SetDllDirectory, restricted LoadLibraryEx flags, signature validation, or digest validation was found for this loader.
The scanner routes themselves do not provide authentication or authorization, although their server is loopback-bound.
盲点
The checkout contains no built scanner-bridge.exe or concrete release package, so actual packaged DLL placement and signatures could not be inspected.
Repository artifacts do not define production Windows ACLs for the D: path, application directory, current directory, or other DLL search locations.
The repository does not establish whether Project-X is ever launched elevated, as a Windows service, or under a dedicated account with access unavailable to local attackers.
No Windows runtime, Wine environment, Windows SDK, or cross-toolchain was available to execute a proof DLL.
The effective Windows DLL search order can vary with OS configuration and process-wide settings outside the repository.
External reverse-proxy or tunnel configuration is not present in the checkout; however, remote triggering alone would not provide the required local DLL write.
title: Untrusted DLL search can hijack Scanner Bridge

comments: The Electron startup path now points to `<userData>/data/answer-card` instead of the location used by existing installations, with no migration before passing it to the server.
The standalone default is also relocated, and initialization simply creates empty cards, assets, and layouts directories at the new location rather than detecting or migrating the legacy tree.

Data-directory relocation hides existing answer cards
严重级别
Informational
